IsAllowed.maps_to: is_allowed (sts2_rl/relics/dragon_fruit.py:14) -> is_before_act3_treasure_chest (sts2_rl/relics/base.py:82-84), consulted by RunState._drop_disallowed_from_grab_bag (sts2_rl/run.py:769) before every pool pull
IsAllowed.issue: Closed 2026-07-27: pool eligibility is modelled now. `Relic.is_allowed(run)` exists on the sim's base (sts2_rl/relics/base.py:198, default True) and this relic overrides it with `is_before_act3_treasure_chest(run)` (sts2_rl/relics/dragon_fruit.py:14), the `TotalFloor < 41` predicate of RelicModel.IsBeforeAct3TreasureChest (RelicModel.cs:452-456). RunState._drop_disallowed_from_grab_bag (sts2_rl/run.py:769) applies it before EVERY pull and REMOVES the rejects from the bag -- pull_relic_from_front (run.py:731), pull_relic_from_back (run.py:752) and the Shop-rarity bag (run.py:783) are the only three pull paths -- mirroring RelicGrabBag.RemoveDisallowedRelicsFromDeques (RelicGrabBag.cs:218-270), and `Relic.is_allowed_at_neow` now DELEGATES to is_allowed (sts2_rl/relics/base.py:211-222 = RelicModel.cs:443-446) so the Neow pools (sts2_rl/events/neow.py:72) cannot read a stale flag. Verified by execution against today's code: every one of the 17 cluster members returns is_allowed False at total_floor 60 and True at floor 0. WAS: the sim's Relic base declared no is_allowed member at all and populate_relic_grab_bags shuffled the pool once at run init with no per-pull filter, so the relic stayed pullable for the whole run and a late pull also shifted every subsequent pull.

guards.what: G1 (LIVE): the 'no gold system' premise is FALSE -- the sim has RunState.gold, RunState.gain_gold and a rewards screen that banks gold through it (PROMPT.md bug class 12)
guards.issue: MECHANISM: DragonFruit.cs:22-29 grants MaxHpVar(1) on every gold gain by its owner. The port implements nothing. THE PREMISE IS FALSE, and this is the same false premise batch 1 already disproved for relic/amethyst_aubergine ('the sim has no gold'), which .superpowers/sdd/content-relic-sweeps.md sweep C lists in the same family: the sim has RunState.gold (run.py:152), RunState.gain_gold (run.py:325-333) with a live Hook.ModifyGoldGained chain, twelve ported events that call it, and a reward screen that banks combat gold through it (rewards.py:464, :485). REACHABILITY (LIVE, executed -- py audit/tools/relic_probes_b04.py stubs): `run.gain_gold(25)` moves gold 99 -> 124 and leaves max_hp at 80 both with and without the relic, where C# gives 81. Both sides ported and no unported content needed: Dragon Fruit is Shop rarity in the transcribed grab bag (relic_pools.py:65 'RELIC.DRAGON_FRUIT'), and gold is gained after essentially every combat, so the relic would be paying out several times per act. IMPLEMENTATION NOTE: unlike relic/dollys_mirror's stub this needs a NEW base hook -- executed, `hasattr(Relic, 'after_gold_gained')` is False, and sweep C explicitly EXCLUDED AfterGoldGained from its 33 one-relic fixes for that reason. Two details of the C# dispatch that the hook must reproduce, both read off PlayerCmd.GainGold: AfterGoldGained fires AFTER `player.Gold += amount` (PlayerCmd.cs:168-169), so the relic sees the new balance; and it is behind the `if (!(amount > 0m)) return;` bail at PlayerCmd.cs:146-149, so a player who also holds relic/ectoplasm (which zeroes the gain) gets NO Max HP -- getting that wrong would turn the two relics from an anti-synergy into a combo. RULE 7: run.py, rewards.py, relic_pools.py, relics/base.py and PlayerCmd.cs are not hashed here.

guards.what: N1: MaxHpVar(1m) read as BaseValue (DragonFruit.cs:15, 27) and the `player == base.Owner` guard (:24)
guards.rationale: No AscensionHelper.GetValueIfAscension in the file, so 1 is the pinned non-ascension value; the sim transcribes no constant at all, which is guard G1's subject rather than a separate numeric error. The owner clause is the multiplayer per-player filter the shared contract puts out of scope -- but it is worth naming for the fix, because Hook.ModifyGoldGained/AfterGoldGained are dispatched over the RUN's listeners for a NAMED player (PlayerCmd.cs:144, :169) and a sim hook that took no player argument would be indistinguishable from the C# behaviour in single-player only.
